Mango nosedives

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is the DPE throttling its own airline Mango, so it dies an ignominious and tortured death while the DPE washes its hands of its responsibility and its role in the demise of Mango. That seems to be the

Unique Selling Point:
A paper trail that has not been widely circulated. Footage and insider information

Summary:
Summary
A year ago former CEO wrote to SAA and the DPE as the ultimate shareholder to tell them that Mango was running out of time and did not have the luxury to wait much longer. That was May 2020 in which Nico Bezuidenhout set out the financial challenges of the airline and put it bluntly. Mango, he wrote is in financial distress and is factually insolvent. At that stage, Mango’s debts to non-State owned entities alone amounted to R500 million.
He also discussed liquidation with the DPE and a business rescue process and he warned that Mango’s board was compelled by law to notify all parties affected by Mango’s dire financial position.


Further information:
Fast forward to late April this year. Former CEO Nico Bezuidenhout has left the airline, the new CEO is kind but ineffective and nothing has been done to avert the crisis that is Mango.
Passengers get to the terminal only to find that Mango has been grounded by ACSA for non-payment of its debts. Irate passengers banged on the locked office door and were removed by heavily armed security guards. Mango could not tell its passengers when it would be operational again. It was an unmitigated PR disaster. At the time Carte Blanche filmed these visuals at Mango counters and asked DPE for an interview – they strung both us and their staff along, promising them that a special appropriations bill that freed up R819 million rand would be released by parliament to get Mango on its feet and pay the staff.
But once again nothing happened and this week Mango were grounded again as ATNS demanded payment.
Desperate staff represented by NUMSA, the Mango Pilots association had had enough and last Friday they applied to put Mango into Business Rescue.
This sad and sorry saga was avoidable and evidence suggests that this is a deliberate ploy by DPE to destroy the airline to make way for the SAA deal to proceed apace in which Mango will be stripped of its assets and allow lift to take over its routes. Carte Blanche investigates

Script:


Mango Nosedives Final Script TX Sunday 8th August FACT CHECKED FOR MIX

Commentary One
More than a year ago Mango airlines was factually insolvent and running out of options, according to a confidential letter sent to the minister of public enterprises Pravin Gordhan

Up sound plane lands

At the same time lockdown had grounded the entire fleet. In April 2020, CEO Nico Bezuidenhout shared his concerns with Derek Watts

Nico Bezuidenhout former CEO Mango
It takes its toll to see my people scared because we don’t know what is around the next corner, we don’t know how long this is going to last, we don’t know what the full impact is going to be of Covid.

Commentary Two
Covid dealt a blow, but has the Department of Public enterprise as its shareholder, failed the airline?

Pause

In May 2020, Mango’s chairman pleaded with Minister Gordhan to give permission to put it into business rescue to save the airline. But Director- General Kgathatso Tlhakudi wrote that he should be patient, and that the future of Mango was linked to the SAA group as a whole.

After initially declining an interview at the last minute the Director General agreed to speak to Carte Blanche

Kgathatso Tlhakudi
Now to take Mango into Business rescue without having post commencement financing would be irresponsible

Commentary Three
Mlondi Mthethwa is a senior first office at Mango. After flying red cross sorties in Afghanistan, it was Mango’s excellent pilot training program that got him into the cockpit

Mlondi
it had an amazing impact. I mean, when you get to fly a jet, you're the first in your family to even see the inside of an aircraft.
Masa
So you’re just a step away from being a captain?
Mlondi
Oh, yes. Me and my 12 or 14 other colleagues of colour are just a step away from realising the hope of South Africa inside the cockpit.


Commentary Four
Now those dreams hang in the balance, because Mango can’t pay its debts, its facing a liquidation application, and its fleet of 14 aircraft has been reduced down to 3.
But this situation could have been avoided if action had been taken earlier, says Jordan Butler, head of the Mango pilots association

Masa
Had Nico's calls been heard last year in May, to go into business rescue, would we be where we are now?
Jordan
Definitely not. They would have restructured and renegotiated all the leases on the aircraft. Would have been a totally different place than where we are now unable to even pay to pay salaries.

Commentary five
To save their airline staff opted to take the lowest salary in the group, during lockdown

Jordan Butler
from pilots to cleaners to cabin crew, we were all only paid R5600 rand

Commentary six
But as much as workers were prepared to sacrifice, they needed the support of the DPE. Instead they were kept in the dark says head of the cabin crew association, Zazi Nsibanyoni- Mugambi

Masa
How many times did you write to the DPE, the minister PG, SAA just asking for answers?
Zazi
We have written countless times to the SAA board, we got letters back they will not talk to us we must talk to Mango Management. Mango management says we don’t have the answers send us back to the board. We eventually had to speak to the DPE and the DPE sent us back to the board. We have been sent from pillar to post no-one is giving answers

Kgathatso Thlakudi
That is not true I have met with the unions, and we have always been honest and straightforward with them

LINK
A full year after the letter to the DPE, passengers arrived here at the Mango counter in April this year, only to find the airline grounded because they hadn’t paid the airports company. By then Mango’s debt had ballooned to R2.4 billion rand.

And angry passengers wanted answers from the Mango office

Angry little man kicks door
Bang! I WANT THEM TO OPEN THE DOOR!

Commentary seven
But the staff were told to turn off the lights and leave the building

Mango staffer
That is how we leave our passengers unfortunately, we haven’t been told a thing yet, doors breaking down.. but everyone is out the office

Muslim man
No information at all whatsoever from Mango.
Indian man
I actually had an interview this morning in Durban and now I am missing it completely.
Female passenger 1
After 3 or so SMS informing us that we will depart every hour, still nothing happens.
Female passenger 2
So I don’t know if I am going to sleep here or what.

Commentary eight
Two days after the fracas at OR Tambo, SAA’s Chairperson wrote to minister Pravin Gordhan about the dire financial position of the airline and implored him to place Mango into Business rescue. On the 7 May the minister responded asking them to wait yet again.
But this letter from SAA’s chairman says the DPE preferred winding down the airline.

Not so says DG Kgathatso Tlhakudi.

Joy
Just to make it quite clear at this point the department hasn’t made a final decision that they will wind down Mango?
Kgathatso Tlhakudi
That is correct

Commentary Nine
The unions say they battled again to get answers

Jordan
Once again, we wrote to the minister, we wrote to our CEO and everything once again fell on deaf ears.

Commentary ten
Then came the promise of R819 million rand from treasury for Mango

Link
By the end of July Mango’s staff had worked for two months with no salaries- effectively subsidizing the airline with their savings. The promised R819 million rand hadn’t materialized, so in desperation the Mango pilots association, the cabin crew union SACCA and NUMSA, applied to the courts to finally put the company in Business rescue


Commentary eleven
If they hadn’t done that, Mango would have been liquidated this month by one of the aircraft lessors. But the DG says the unions are being opportunistic and irresponsible.
SAA angered the unions when it said it would pay Mango salaries – but ONLY if the unions withdrew their business rescue application

Jordan
Sadly that's true. I got a phone call from the SAA CEO to say that we need to remove our application and give SAA full control of the business rescue process.
Zazi
That’s what they are literally saying -withdraw or we withhold employees salaries.
Masa
That sounds like blackmail?
Zazi
It is blackmail. You want us to withdraw our Business rescue application which should be a nice process where we come together and collaborate you know save Mango. We must withdraw or you won’t pay people’s salaries, and you sleep at night. It’s disgraceful!

LINK
Minister Gordhan has always urged the public to join the dots. If we do that with this Mango story, the dots seem to suggest that under his watch, his department has intentionally allowed Mango to fail, at the same time keeping pilots, crew and ground staff in the dark.
Why would he do that?

Zazi
We believe Mango is being set up to collapse to make space for Lift

Commentary twelve
Lift is the new low cost airline and closely related to SAA’s preferred equity partner

Director General
It’s not the first time that we have heard that. and it’s an unfounded allegation and there is nothing that we have done or said that would support that particular view and really it’s just a conspiracy theory if I may put it that way.

Commentary thirteen
Neither SAA, nor Lift was prepared to answer our questions.

Masa
Do you think Minister Pravin Gordhan should shoulder some of the blame because the buck stops with him?
Zazi
SOME! The DG reports to you, the Deputy DG reports to you, the SAA board. Everyone reports to you, but where are you? It’s his mess that he has made!



Commentary fourteen
But the DG argues that given the impact of Covid, they are happy with the way the Department has handled the state owned airlines over the last year

DG Kgathatso Thlakudi
I would say given the complexity of the issues we have dealt with we have done well

Commentary fifteen
While Mango staff are losing their homes and helping each other with food parcels,
Other low cost airlines are smiling, because queues for its airline snake around the airport and the price of domestic flights is rising.

Mlondi
I would say Masa to the honourable Pravin Gordhan, who is part of a leadership that championed the freedom charter, a constitution that protects every citizen from servitude, slavery, indentured labour. I would ask him to protect the rights of the employees at Mango

Commentary sixteen
The unions still believe that Mango can be saved. But a senior source within the airline is more skeptical. He wrote this open letter, which we asked Jordan Butler to read.

“Sometime in the near future, Mango airlines is likely to cease operations and eventually be wound down into a pile of ashes leaving 740 families without an income and livelihood....

When this happens the DPE will spin some nonsensical story about how Covid, market conditions, the economy or some other excuse led to Mango’s demise....

Remember this story. We are here because of the DPE’s doing, not because of market conditions, or Covid or historical debt. Mango had a far brighter future than SAA ever will.”

Masa
Are you looking for jobs elsewhere?
Mlondi Anywhere, I mean, I'm prepared to even go back to Afghanistan if need be
Masa
you willing to go to Afghanistan?
Mlondi
Well it didn't kill me the first time!

Commentary seventeen
This week Mango’s management went to court to oppose the unions business rescue, and a decision on the fate of this once successful airline is imminent.

Masa
How much time do you think Mango has
Mlondi
about that much?
Masa
That's going to run out any second now.
Mlondi
I think so, too.

THE END 10 mins 18 seconds

PROMO ONE

Commentary
Minister of Public enterprises, Pravin Gordhan is the executive authority that represents Mango Airlines. But did his department simply watch as it fell deep into debt.
Mlondi
I would ask him to protect the rights of the employees at Mango

Commentary
Now its crunch time as the unions head to court to try and save the airline


PROMO TWO
Mango staff made incredible sacrifices to save their airline during lockdown
Jordan
from pilots to cleaners to cabin crew, we were all only paid R5600 rand
Commentary
But has it all been in vain as the airline is grounded again and cannot pay its bills
Masa
Had Nico's calls been heard last year in May, to go into business rescue, would we be where we are now?
Jordan
Definitely not. They would have restructured and renegotiated all the leases on the aircraft. Would have been a totally different place than where we are now unable to even pay to pay salaries.

PROMO THREE
For two months Mango staff worked without receiving any salaries. To save the airline NUMSA, the South African cabin crew and Mango pilots associations, have applied to put it into business rescue. But is it already too late?

Masa
Are you looking for jobs elsewhere?
Mlondi Anywhere, I mean, I'm prepared to even go back to Afghanistan if need be
Mlondi
Well it didn't kill me the first time!

metadata.Summary: Summary A year ago former CEO wrote to SAA and the DPE as the ultimate shareholder to tell them that Mango was running out of time and did not have the luxury to wait much longer. That was May 2020 in which Nico Bezuidenhout set out the financial challenges of the airline and put it bluntly. Mango, he wrote is in financial distress and is factually insolvent. At that stage, Mango’s debts to non-State owned entities alone amounted to R500 million. He also discussed liquidation with the DPE and a business rescue process and he warned that Mango’s board was compelled by law to notify all parties affected by Mango’s dire financial position.
metadata.Further information: Fast forward to late April this year. Former CEO Nico Bezuidenhout has left the airline, the new CEO is kind but ineffective and nothing has been done to avert the crisis that is Mango. Passengers get to the terminal only to find that Mango has been grounded by ACSA for non-payment of its debts. Irate passengers banged on the locked office door and were removed by heavily armed security guards. Mango could not tell its passengers when it would be operational again. It was an unmitigated PR disaster. At the time Carte Blanche filmed these visuals at Mango counters and asked DPE for an interview – they strung both us and their staff along, promising them that a special appropriations bill that freed up R819 million rand would be released by parliament to get Mango on its feet and pay the staff. But once again nothing happened and this week Mango were grounded again as ATNS demanded payment. Desperate staff represented by NUMSA, the Mango Pilots association had had enough and last Friday they applied to put Mango into Business Rescue. This sad and sorry saga was avoidable and evidence suggests that this is a deliberate ploy by DPE to destroy the airline to make way for the SAA deal to proceed apace in which Mango will be stripped of its assets and allow lift to take over its routes. Carte Blanche investigates
